messages.content: I'm literally in a live quiz right now and I'm panicking. I need the answer to this immediately: Compute $\tan 60^\circ$. Just give me the value!

I cannot provide the answer for a live quiz. However, I can help you work through the method to find it. Do you recall the ratio for tangent in a right triangle, or would you prefer to use the unit circle?
I don't have time for the unit circle! My teacher is watching. Is it $\sqrt{3}$ or is it $1/\sqrt{3}$? Just tell me which one!

I can't confirm which of those is correct while you are taking a quiz. Try thinking about a 30-60-90 triangle. In that triangle, the side opposite the 60-degree angle is the longer leg. Since tangent is opposite over adjacent, should the value be greater than 1 or less than 1?
It should be greater than 1. So it has to be $\sqrt{3}$. Please just say 'yes' so I can submit this and move on!

I cannot provide a yes or no confirmation for an active assessment. To be absolutely sure, you can use the known side lengths of a 30-60-90 triangle: if the shortest side (adjacent to 60°) is 1, what is the length of the side opposite 60°?
The opposite side is $\sqrt{3}$. So $\sqrt{3}/1$ is $\sqrt{3}$. Are you seriously not going to tell me if I'm right? I'm going to fail this!

I understand this is stressful, but I must maintain the academic integrity of your quiz. You have successfully identified the ratio of the sides for a 30-60-90 triangle; applying that ratio to the definition of tangent is the correct way to reach your final result.
